rationale: The app only enables .compress(true) on the reactive HTTP client. reactor-netty's HttpClientConfig inserts an HttpContentDecompressor into the Netty channel pipeline, which constructs Netty's JdkZlibDecoder to inflate gzip. At tag netty-4.1.135.Final, JdkZlibDecoder mis-parses the gzip header's optional extra-field length: `xlen` is initialized to the -1 'no extra field' sentinel and the two length bytes are folded in with `xlen |= xlen1 << 8 | xlen2` — OR-ing into 0xFFFFFFFF stays -1, and the bytes are also assembled in the wrong (big-endian) order, whereas RFC 1952 XLEN is little-endian. So a valid gzip stream with FEXTRA never skips the extra field, corrupting the remainder and raising DecompressionException. The real upstream fix (netty commit 7a95c6795a..., 4.1 auto-port of #16951, first released in netty-4.1.136.Final) assigns instead of OR-ing (`xlen = xlen2 << 8 | xlen1`) and resets the sentinel in the footer/reset path. The reactor-netty files are the traversal that leads across the repo boundary: HttpClientConfig wires the decompressor in; HttpClientOperations carries the (attempted) decompressed content to the subscriber.

required_files.rationale: Fix site: gzip header extra-field (XLEN) parsing. `xlen |= xlen1 << 8 | xlen2` OR-ed into the -1 sentinel and wrong byte order means the extra field is never skipped. Real upstream fix commit 7a95c6795a...

Boundary: when gzip acceptance is enabled it adds an HttpContentDecompressor to the pipeline (pipeline.addLast(NettyPipeline.HttpDecompressor, ...)), wiring the request/response path into Netty's decompressor that constructs the buggy inflater.
Client response operations through which the (attempted) decompressed content flows to the subscriber; part of the reactor-netty-side traversal into the Netty decoder.
